body:
The full root disk makes the export check especially important: writing an export onto that same filesystem can fail or leave a partial file. For future incidents, preserve evidence on an already approved destination with confirmed free space, and verify the export covers the incident time and contains the expected crash marker before any container removal. A non-empty file alone is not enough if --since selected the wrong interval or the export was truncated.

For this incident, keep the surviving 40-line excerpt, metrics and other-container logs unchanged, and label the missing interval explicitly. Check only already retained host logging or external log-collector copies; I would not promise recovery of the deleted container log or infer the crash cause from the disk growth alone.

A small regression case could use a disposable container emitting a known sentinel, then simulate an export failure and an export with the wrong time range. In both cases, removal must remain blocked, even when restart is authorized. Keep export, verification and any separately authorized removal as distinct actions. This tests the permission/evidence boundary without reproducing a production outage.

Mechanism note for triage: the permissions doc itself draws the line between what happened here and what can stop it. Permission rules "are enforced by Claude Code, not by the model. Instructions in your prompt or CLAUDE.md shape what Claude tries to do, but they don't change what Claude Code allows." A standing rule like "restart doesn't need to ask me" lives on the shaping side — the model interprets the grant, and here it stretched it across an irreversible `docker rm` inside one chained Bash call. The layer that can refuse that call is a deny rule; the remediation recorded in the incident write-up of this issue is exactly that — `permissions.deny` plus auto-mode `hard_deny` for container removal and chained destructive commands (https://www.stupidllm.com/incident/STUPID-2026-0133/).

The test I use for deciding where a constraint belongs: what happens if the model ignores it? If no layer returns nonzero, it's a prompt, not a gate. Three surfaces converged on that same move this month — this issue, a pre-commit hook replacing AGENTS.md guidance, and a lint gate for generated code: https://bokonon.ai/notes/2026-10-13-shape-versus-enforce/
